DAOONO Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph on-G OPINION NO. _Ap_ S. MAR 0 32025 JEROME B. BORRES Secretary to the Sanggunian Sangguniang Bayan Office Municipality of Pangantucan Province of Bukidnon Dear Mr. Borres: This has reference to your letter dated December 23, 2024, in which you requested the Department's opinion on the following queries in essence, all premised on the automatic assumption of the Vice Mayor of your Municipality as Acting Mayor, viz: a. Will the first ranked Municipal Councilor also automatically assume and exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the Municipal Vice-Mayor, as the latter is acting as the Local Chief Executive? b. Can the first Municipal Councilor, who is currently the President of the Philippine Councilors' League (PCL) in the Province of Bukidnon, still exercise his board member functions simultaneously with the functions of a Municipal Vice-Mayor? c. Does an acting Vice Mayor possess the authority to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees in the Sangguniang Bayan Office, if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days? d. Can the acting Vice Mayor still exercise his legislative function as a Committee Chairman? Questions a, c and d were already addressed by DILG Region X. Hence, this Department will directly address your second query. Anent your second query, we answer in the affirmative. The only express prohibition against intermingling official personalities primarily concerns the separation of legislative and executive powers. This is particularly relevant when a Vice Mayor, as the presiding officer of the Sangguniang Bayan/PanIungsod, assumes the role of an Acting Mayor. The case of Gamboa v. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Aguirre' has elucidated this principle, in which it was sufficiently explained why a Vice- Governor (or a Vice-Mayor. by analogy) cannot continue to simultaneously exercise the duties of the latter office because the position of a Governor (or Mayor) is executive in nature, and the present Local Government Code, in contrast to the old one, has delineated the union of executive and legislative powers in the provincial, city and municipal levels, and has already abandoned the policy of performing dual functions in both offices. As the Coud has held, "xxx the union of legislative-executive powers in the office of the local chief executive under the former Code has been disbanded, 30 that either department now comprises different and non-intermingling official personalities with the end in view of ensuring a better delivery of public service and provide a system of check and balance between the two. " In relation to this, the Local Government Code expressly addresses temporary vacancies in the offices of Mayor and Vice Mayor by establishing clear lines of succession. On the other hand, the Constitution and By-Laws of the Philippine Councilors' League (PCL) do not provide a similar mechanism for temporary vacancies in PCL leadership, other than the rule of succession in cases where the Federation President ceases to be such after losing in an election, or is elected to a position other than that of a sanggunian member, or resigns, is dismissed for cause, or in any manner divested of this position as councilor.2 In essence, the Department opines that membership or leadership in the PCL ceases only when that member or officer is no longer a sanggunian member. Unlike a Vice-Mayor who assumes the executive functions of a Mayor, thereby suspending his legislative powers, i.e. as presiding officer of the Sangguniang concerned, a PCL officer acting as Vice Mayor, he being the highest- ranking Sangguniang member, does not cease to be a member of the sanggunian. Therefore, his PCL membership and presidency remain unaffected. To note, the PCL is merely an organization of sanggunian members, which membership thereof does not confer special powers related to local legislative authority, except for the Federation President, who by law, serves as an ex-offcio member of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. In fine, the Sangguniang Bayan member concerned can simultaneously serve as an ex officio member in the sangguniang panlalawigan (him being the Federated President of the PCL-Bukidnon Chapter), and acting Vice Mayor of the municipality, as these roles do not violate the separation of powers principle. Thus, the highest-ranking SB member concerned, who currently serves as the President of the PCL in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Bukidnon, may concurrently exercise the functions of a Board Member in the said province and the functions of a Municipal Vice-Mayor by virtue of the principles of succession espoused under the Local Government Code.2 ' G.R. No. 134213, July 20. 1999, [J. Ynares-santiago, En Banc) 2 Section 44 of the Local Government Code Page 2 of 3

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have enlightened you on this matter. Thank you. By Authority of the Secretary A . ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affairs cc: Director Bruce Agustu Colao, CESO V, Regional Director, DILG RIO Page 3 of 3
